## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-buyer-commissioned

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: a QoE the buyer commissioned, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A lender may have a QoE the buyer commissioned reviewed by one of its approved vendors instead of ordering a new one.
- **Quote:** "Recognizing that some Applicant buyers may elect to commission their own QoE prior to engaging with the Lender for financing as part of their own due diligence, Lenders may elect to have that report reviewed by one of their approved vendors to help mitigate costs."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-cash-proof

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE cash proof, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** An SBA-required QoE must include a cash proof that reconciles bank statements to the income statement and tax returns, for the trailing 12 months and the last two fiscal years.
- **Quote:** "The QoE must include a Cash Proof. For purposes of this requirement, a Cash Proof is a financial analysis that reconstructs cash receipts and disbursements by reconciling bank statement data to the income statement and tax return for each period under review. The Cash Proof is designed to identify discrepancies in income and undisclosed expenses and must be performed on both a trailing 12-month basis and the last two fiscal years."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-dsc

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE findings drive debt service coverage, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** When a QoE is required, the lender calculates debt coverage from its findings and must reduce the loan if coverage doesn't support the deal.
- **Quote:** "When a change of ownership transaction requires a Quality of Earnings (QoE) report as part of the necessary financial due diligence, the Lender must use the report’s findings to calculate the Debt Service Coverage. If that Debt Service Coverage does not support the business valuation and proposed debt structure, the loan amount must be reduced accordingly."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-not-for-seller

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE performed for the lender, not the seller, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** An SBA-required quality of earnings report must be independent, done for the lender, and not prepared by or for the seller.
- **Quote:** "The QoE must be performed by an independent, experienced financial professional and must be conducted for the benefit of the Lender. As the QoE report is part of the financial due diligence of the transaction, the report must not be prepared by or for the seller."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-owner-buyout-exempt

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE not required for owner buyouts and ESOPs, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The SBA QoE requirement does not apply to owner buyouts or ESOP and cooperative transactions.
- **Quote:** "Owner Buyout and ESOP & Cooperative transactions are not subject to the QoE requirement because the existing owner(s) retain operational knowledge of the business and the transaction does not result in a change to the management or operating structure."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-revenue-quality

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE add-backs and revenue quality, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** An SBA-required QoE must document every add-back and assess revenue quality, including customer concentration and contract continuity.
- **Quote:** "The report must identify and document all add-backs and adjustments to the seller's reported earnings, including non-recurring revenue or expenses, above- or below-market owner compensation, related-party transactions, deferred maintenance, and accounting methodology differences between cash-basis and accrual-basis reporting. The QoE must assess the quality and sustainability of the business's revenue base, including customer concentration risk, contract continuity, and the likelihood that existing revenue and margins will be maintained post-sale."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-special-purpose

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE and special purpose property, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** No QoE is required when the acquisition involves an owner-occupied special purpose property, whatever the price.
- **Quote:** "A Quality of Earnings report is not required for a transaction involving the acquisition of an owner-occupied Special Purpose Property, regardless of the Business Purchase Price."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-threshold

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: Quality of Earnings required at $3 million, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For 7(a) initial acquisitions and business expansions with a business purchase price of $3 million or more, the lender must obtain a quality of earnings report as well as the business valuation, measured before equity, seller debt or other financing.
- **Quote:** "For Business Expansion and Initial Acquisition transactions where the Purchase Price as defined in Paragraph A.1 is equal to or greater than $3 million, the Lender must also obtain a Quality of Earnings (QoE) in addition to the required Business Valuation. The $3 million threshold is determined before the application of buyer equity, seller debt, or other financing sources."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
